design.text: Open-label, randomized (2:1), controlled, multi-center trial of tebentafusp versus investigator's choice (dacarbazine, ipilimumab, or pembrolizumab), stratified by LDH status.

citations.quote: This is an ongoing open-label, randomized, multi-center study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tebentafusp versus investigator's choice (dacarbazine, ipilimumab, or pembrolizumab) in adult HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with mUM who had not received prior systemic therapy in the metastatic setting.

Enrolled patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either tebentafusp (Arm1) or investigator's choice (Arm 2), the latter of which was selected prior to randomization. Randomization was stratified by LDH status.

indication.text: KIMMTRAK is indicated for the treatment of HLA-A*02:01-positive adult patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma.

target_moa.text: Tebentafusp is a bispecific gp100 peptide-HLA-directed CD3 T cell engager; its TCR arm binds a gp100 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on uveal melanoma cells and its anti-CD3 arm redirects polyclonal T cells to lyse the gp100-expressing tumor cells.

citations.quote: Tebentafusp-tebn (referred to as tebentafusp) is a bispecific gp100 peptide-HLA-directed CD3 T cell engager. The tumor cell receptor arm of tebentafusp binds to a gp100 peptide presented by human leukocyte antigen-A*02:01 (HLA-A*02:01) on the cell surface of uveal melanoma tumor cells.

In vitro, tebentafusp-tebn bound to HLA-A*02:01-positive uveal melanoma cells and activated polyclonal T cells to release inflammatory cytokines and cytolytic proteins, which results in direct lysis of uveal melanoma tumor cells.

modality.text: Bispecific fusion protein (soluble TCR fused to an anti-CD3 scFv).

citations.quote: Tebentafusp (IMCgp100) is a bispecific fusion protein that consists of a soluble T cell receptor (TCR) fused to an anti-cluster of differentiation 3 (anti-CD3) single-chain variable fragment (scFv).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 30%) were cytokine release syndrome, rash, pyrexia, pruritus, fatigue, nausea, chills, abdominal pain, edema, hypotension, dry skin, headache, and vomiting. CRS occurred in 89% of KIMMTRAK patients (0.8% Grade 3/4) and rash in 83% (18% Grade 3/4). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 28% of patients; one patient (0.4%) had a fatal reaction (pulmonary embolism).

detail.text: Patients are selected based on a positive HLA-A*02:01 genotyping test; the SeCore® HLA Sequencing System and uTYPE® Dx v1.0 HLA Sequence Analysis Software (Thermo Fisher Scientific) were used to identify HLA-A*02:01-positive patients, though an FDA-approved test was not available at approval.

citations.quote: Select patients for treatment of unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma with KIMMTRAK based on a positive HLA-A*02:01 genotyping test [*see Clinical Studies (14)*]. An FDA-approved test for the detection of HLA-A*02:01 genotyping is not currently available.

The SeCore® HLA Sequencing System and uTYPE® Dx v1.0 HLA Sequence Analysis Software developed by Thermo Fisher Scientific have been used as a companion diagnostic (CDx) to identify HLA-A*02:01 positive patients for tebentafusp clinical studies.

requirement.text: 4180-1: Conduct an assay validation study to demonstrate the assay can accurately differentiate HLA-A*02:01 from other HLA A alleles to identify patients who may benefit, to support an FDA-approved companion diagnostic HLA typing assay patient selection test.

citations.quote: 4180-1 Conduct an assay validation study to demonstrate that the assay can accurately differentiate HLA-A*02:01 from other HLA A alleles for identification of patients with uveal melanoma who may benefit from treatment with Kimtrak (tebentafusp-tebn) and use the data to support an FDA approved companion diagnostic HLA typing assay patient selection test.

requirement.text: 4180-2: Determine the presence of neutralizing anti-drug antibodies against Kimmtrak in all patient samples that tested positive for binding ADA in studies IMCgp100-202 and IMCgp100-102, and assess the clinical impact on PK, efficacy and safety.
